title: Longest Value Streak

statement.markdown:
Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest run of **consecutive integer values** present in it (order and duplicates in the array don't matter).

Sorting gives O(n log n). The interview follow-up is to do it in O(n) — think about which numbers can *start* a streak.

examples.explanation: The values 1, 2, 3, 4 form a streak of length 4.

hints: Put everything in a set. Now membership is O(1) — what would you look up?
A value v starts a streak only if v−1 is NOT in the set. Only count upward from those starters.
Every value is visited at most twice (once in the scan, once inside a streak walk) — that's the O(n) argument.
solutionExplanation: Load the values into a set, then only walk streaks from their left endpoints — values v where v−1 is absent. Each streak is walked exactly once, so despite the nested-looking loop the total work is O(n). The 'only start at starters' insight is the whole problem.
